topicName: Git Hooks: Client-Side and Server-Side Hooks
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Git Hooks: Client-Side and Server-Side"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Git hooks are scripts that Git executes before or after events such as commit, push, and receive. They are a powerful tool to automate and customize your Git workflow. Hooks are stored in the '.git/hooks' directory of your Git repository. By default, this directory contains example hook scripts, which are disabled by default (they have a '.sample' extension). To enable a hook, simply remove the '.sample' extension."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Git Hooks"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Git hooks can be categorized into two main types: client-side hooks and server-side hooks."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Client-Side Hooks"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Client-side hooks are triggered by Git operations on the local machine. They are useful for enforcing coding standards, running tests, and preventing commits that don't meet certain criteria. Client-side hooks are local to each repository and are not automatically shared with others."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Client-Side Hooks"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"pre-commit: This hook runs before a commit is made. It's often used to run linters, formatters, or unit tests to ensure code quality."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"prepare-commit-msg: This hook runs before the commit message editor is opened. It can be used to automatically generate or modify the commit message."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"commit-msg: This hook runs after the commit message editor is closed, but before the commit is made. It can be used to validate the commit message format."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"post-commit: This hook runs after a commit is made. It's often used for notifications or other post-commit tasks."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"pre-rebase: This hook runs before a rebase operation. It can be used to prevent rebasing if certain conditions are not met."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"post-checkout: This hook runs after a 'git checkout' command. It can be used to set up the working directory based on the checked-out branch."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"post-merge: This hook runs after a 'git merge' command. It can be used to perform tasks after a merge, such as updating dependencies."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: pre-commit Hook"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's create a simple 'pre-commit' hook that prevents commits with the word 'WIP' (Work In Progress) in the commit message."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"#!/bin/sh

commit_message=$(git log -1 HEAD --pretty=%B)

if echo "$commit_message" | grep -q WIP;
then
  echo "Error: Commit message contains 'WIP'. Please remove it before committing."
  exit 1
fi"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Save this script as '.git/hooks/pre-commit' and make it executable:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, if you try to commit with a message containing 'WIP', the commit will be aborted."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Server-Side Hooks"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Server-side hooks run on the Git server. They are useful for enforcing policies, automating deployments, and integrating with other systems. Server-side hooks are shared among all users of the repository."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Server-Side Hooks"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"pre-receive: This hook runs when the server receives a push, but before any refs are updated. It can be used to validate the incoming changes."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"update: This hook runs for each ref being updated. It can be used to enforce branch-specific policies."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"post-receive: This hook runs after all refs have been updated. It's often used for deployment or notification tasks."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: pre-receive Hook"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's create a simple 'pre-receive' hook that prevents pushing directly to the 'main' branch. This encourages the use of pull requests."},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"#!/bin/sh

while read oldrev newrev refname
do
  branch=$(git rev-parse --symbolic --abbrev-ref $refname)

  if [ "$branch" = "main" ]; then
    echo "Error: Pushing directly to 'main' branch is not allowed. Use pull requests."
    exit 1
  fi
done"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Save this script as '.git/hooks/pre-receive' on the server and make it executable:"},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-receive"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, if someone tries to push directly to the 'main' branch, the push will be rejected."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Important Considerations"},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Client-side hooks are not automatically shared. Each developer needs to set them up in their local repository."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Server-side hooks require access to the server's file system and appropriate permissions."},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hooks can be written in any scripting language (e.g., Shell, Python, Ruby) as long as the Git server or the client machine can execute them."},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be mindful of the performance impact of hooks, especially on the server-side. Long-running hooks can slow down Git operations."},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"Git hooks are a powerful tool for customizing and automating your Git workflow. By understanding the different types of hooks and how to use them, you can improve code quality, enforce policies, and streamline your development process."}]
